title: High-Q superconducting microwave resonators using MBE titanium nitride
authors: Anand Ithepalli, Haoran Lu, Eegene Clara Chung, Xiangqin Wang, Amit Rohan Rajapurohita, Keun-Yeol Park, Celesta S. Chang, Peter McMahon, Huili Grace Xing, David Muller, Valla Fatemi, Debdeep Jena
abstract: Using molecular beam epitaxy, we have realized thin films of titanium nitride (TiN) on c-plane sapphire that exhibit the lowest observed full-width at half maximum X-ray rocking curve width of 18 arcsec. Though the (111) oriented TiN exhibits an abrupt and crystalline interface with sapphire, for the first time we observe sub-surface defects in the sapphire substrate, which nucleate structural defects in the epitaxial TiN layer. Using quarter-wavelength coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonators in a 3 \textmu m/6 \textmu m/3 \textmu m gap/strip/gap lines in a hanger geometry, we find the internal quality factor of the TiN resonators to be $>10^{6}$ in the single-photon $\langle n \rangle \sim 1$ limit at 5.8 GHz and 10 mK, rising to $>20 \times 10^{6}$ at $\langle n \rangle \sim 10^{6}$. The results are of high interest for applications of superconducting TiN in several areas, and provide a path towards epitaxial Josephson junctions with crystalline barriers in the future for high coherence qubits.
summary: This research reports on the fabrication of high-quality superconducting microwave resonators using epitaxial titanium nitride grown by MBE on sapphire. By achieving state-of-the-art crystalline quality and demonstrating extremely high intrinsic quality factors ($>10^6$), the work provides a robust platform for developing next-generation, high-coherence quantum superconducting circuits.
main_problem: The primary goal is achieving superconducting microwave resonators with extremely high quality factors ($Q$) using epitaxial titanium nitride (TiN) thin films.
main_result: The fabricated TiN resonators achieved internal quality factors exceeding $10^6$ in the single-photon limit, rising to over $20 	imes 10^6$ at higher photon numbers.
method: The study combines advanced epitaxial growth (MBE) for material synthesis with microwave characterization using quarter-wavelength coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonators cooled to milliKelvin temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting circuit built from MBE-grown TiN thin films deposited on c-plane sapphire substrates. The performance is characterized by the resonator's quality factor ($Q_i$) under varying photon occupation numbers ($\langle n angle$).
key_observables: Internal quality factor ($Q_i$), X-ray rocking curve width (FWHM), superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), and energy participation ratios ($	ext{pr}$).
important_parameters: Operating temperatures of $10	ext{ mK}$, microwave frequency of 5.8 GHz, and high quality factor values ($>10^6$).
main_assumptions: The high performance is attributed to the crystalline nature of the TiN film and low intrinsic surface oxide loss tangent, despite observing sub-surface defects in the sapphire substrate.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural characterization (XRD rocking curves showing 18 arcsec FWHM) and electrical measurements (temperature-dependent resistivity and $S_{21}$ data used to extract high $Q$ factors).
paper_structure: The paper details the MBE growth process, characterizes the material structure using STEM/XRD, measures superconducting properties ($T_c$, RRR), and finally reports microwave resonator performance by measuring $Q_i$ in both single-photon and high-photon regimes.
why_interesting: High-$Q$ resonators are fundamental components for superconducting qubits (e.g., transmon or flux qubits) as they dictate coherence times ($T_1$) and coupling strengths, making this work directly relevant to quantum hardware development.
